name: NCP18XH103F03RB
title: NTC thermistors: NCP chips, NXFT and NXRT lead sensors, NTPA inrush current limiters
summary: Murata's NTC thermistor range. NCP chips (0201 to 0805) span 22 Ω to 470 kΩ with B-constants of 3100 to 4500 K for temperature sensing and compensation from -40 °C to +125 °C; NCP18XH103F03RB is the 0603 chip of 10 kΩ ±1%, B25/50 3380 K ±1%. NXFT and NXRT carry a 0402 (1005) element on flexible or stiff leads. NTPA discs of 2.2 to 22 Ω limit the switch-on surge of power supplies, with permissible maximum currents of 1.0 to 5.4 A at 25 °C.

circuits.title: Application circuit, inrush current suppression
circuits.description: An NTPA thermistor sits in the positive DC line between a bridge rectifier and the smoothing electrolytic capacitor. Cold, its resistance limits the charging surge when the supply is switched on; the load current then heats it and its resistance falls.

operation.text: Four families of NTC thermistor share these tables: NCP chips in 0201, 0402, 0603 and 0805 sizes for temperature sensing and compensation; NXFT thermo string sensors, a 0402 element on thin flexible leads 25 to 150 mm long; NXRT lead sensors on stiff 0.4 mm leads 10 to 40 mm long; and NTPA disc thermistors from 7 to 22 mm in diameter for limiting inrush current. All of them comply with EU RoHS (2011/65/EU).

A 0603 (1608) chip of 10 kΩ ±1% at 25 °C with B25/50 = 3380 K ±1% (3428 K for 25-80 °C, 3434 K for 25-85 °C, 3455 K for 25-100 °C), 0.31 mA permissive operating current, 100 mW rated power and a typical dissipation constant of 1 mW/°C, on 4 mm pitch paper tape of 4000. It works from -40 °C to +125 °C.

The chips carry nickel-barrier terminations (silver base, nickel then tin plating). NCP03 and NCP15 are for reflow; NCP18 and NCP21 take flow or reflow. A given resistance keeps the same B-constant across the 0402, 0603 and 0805 sizes. The NCP and NXFT series are UL/cUL recognised under UL1434, file E137188.

Chip and thermo string types: compensating transistors, ICs and crystal oscillators in mobile radios, sensing rechargeable battery temperature, LCD compensation and general circuit compensation. Lead types: battery packs, charge circuits, printer heads, DC fan motors and home appliances. Inrush types: switching power supplies, CRT monitors, colour televisions, VCR supplies and other power circuits, and supplies of less than 100 W.

Measuring current heats the thermistor. On the chips the permissive operating current is the most that keeps the rise to 1 °C; on the NXFT and NXRT sensors the operating current for sensor holds the rise to 0.1 °C. The thermal time constant is the time to cover 63.2% of a step between the starting and the ambient temperature.
The NXFT head is about 1.2 mm on polyurethane-coated 0.3 mm copper wires, twisted (code 1) or not (code 2). It is halogen free: Cl 900 ppm max., Br 900 ppm max., Cl+Br 1500 ppm max.

Solder must not melt inside the resin head. Heat travels up the wire easily when an NXFT lead is cut shorter than 20 mm from the head, or an NXRT lead shorter than 8 mm; NXRT leads are not to be cut below 9 mm. Keep the iron off the head. Do not part the NXFT's paired wires within 10 mm of the head, nor bend a lead to a radius of 1 mm or less. Potting in resin needs its own evaluation. When bending or cutting a lead, hold it on the element side.

In series with the rectified line, the NTPA thermistor's cold resistance limits the surge into the smoothing capacitor; current then heats it, and at its permissible maximum current RT/R25 is about 0.04 to 0.05. The maximum current falls with ambient temperature from 25 °C to zero at 160 °C, and the capacitor must not exceed the permissible value for the type and line voltage. A restart before the part has cooled back to its cold resistance lets more current through.

In operation parts of the NTPA can reach about 160 °C, so nearby parts and materials must stand that heat. The body is not waterproof and must not be immersed in water or solvent for cleaning; its resin coating is not insulation, so keep clearance to other parts. Solder at least 5 mm from the root of the lead, without touching the body with the iron, and do not let preheating melt the internal solder. These parts are meant for switching supplies with smoothing capacitors and are to be run within their maximum current and capacitance.

Lay the chip with its length parallel to the line about which the board flexes, and keep it away from a break-off line: the nearer the perforations and slit, the more strain it takes. Too much solder stresses the chip and can crack it. With flow soldering, a thin or runny adhesive lets the chip lift or slide.

Reflow uses RA or RMA paste; Sn:Pb 63:37 and Sn:Ag:Cu 96.5:3.0:0.5 pastes are used for internal tests. Use rosin flux; avoid strongly acidic flux with more than 0.1 wt% halide and water-soluble flux. Do not wash after using a no-clean flux, keep ultrasonic cleaning from resonating the board, and dry promptly after cleaning.

Store at -10 to +40 °C below 75 %RH without condensation, out of corrosive gas and direct sun, and use within 6 months of delivery, first in first out; reseal lead types after opening. The parts are for ordinary indoor conditions: not corrosive or flammable gas, dust, vacuum or abnormal pressure, wet places, salt water, oils or solvents, or strong vibration. The ceramic is brittle; avoid knocks and heavy pressing.
